title: bug: a candidate-caused dependency-phase refusal (supervisor exit 81) is infra-failure, so the daemon retries it on fresh VMs and escalates with an empty output tail
description: guest-supervisor.py exits 81 for every dependency-phase failure: npm ci out of sync with the protected lockfile, and since CQ-R13 a planted npm-shrinkwrap.json/.npmrc or a missing package.json. npm's output goes to /dev/null, check-session.mjs maps 81 to infra-failure, and packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/repairPolicy.ts retries infra failures, so a candidate that breaks its own install burns the infra retry budget on fresh VMs and the worker never sees why. Split candidate-caused install refusals into a code-failure outcome with a bounded output tail, apart from VM and toolchain faults.
definitionOfDone: A dependency-phase refusal caused by the candidate's files resolves as code-failure with a bounded, sanitized output tail, and is not retried as infra.
A toolchain, cache or VM fault in the same phase stays infra-failure; tests cover both through check-session and the daemon's repair policy.

implementationPlan.description: Test first on the landed 5ed445ca manifest guard and a80f46db host exit-code contract; keep both dependencies. Only three write paths in this plan; check-session.mjs/check-evidence.mjs are the prerequisite's responsibility, and local-runner.test.mjs/CERTIFICATION.md remain CQ-R13-owned. Extend INSTALL/installRun/refusedInstall and KI cases: candidate missing/nonregular package.json, malformed candidate JSON, changed dependency spec/root metadata, overrides/bundle controls, and planted npm-shrinkwrap.json or .npmrc must end with the new supervisor code 82, no stdout frames, no relay, no npm started, no installed bytes. Include valid-first/invalid-second directory and preserve zero installs. Split existing refusedInstall expectations by cause rather than globally changing 81 to 82. Malformed dependency directory list, missing/malformed protected lock/root, toolchain exec/start failures, timeout, offline-cache failure and unknown nonzero npm exit must retain existing infrastructure outcomes, especially exit 81. Protected blob mismatch 79 and reown failures keep their established earlier-phase behavior. Valid install and absent dependency manifest remain unchanged. The new rows must initially fail because the supervisor still collapses all dependency refusals to 81. Retain all previous byte-preservation, no-follow, offline/ignore-scripts/workspaces and cleanup assertions.

Prove the outcome through the real producer and consumers. In local-runner-check.test.mjs reuse C7's SESSION_HARNESS/PY_LOAD/provider-spawn pattern, with INSTALL fixtures and real supervisor main/check_job. Let actual runCheckSession consume the Python child's clean no-frame exit. Table-drive candidate metadata refusal => exactly {outcome:'code-failure', exitCode:82, signal:null, outputTail:<the fixed host diagnostic>}; missing toolchain/cache error/unknown npm exit => infra-failure, never candidate; timeout retains its existing timeout/infra distinction. Assert zero check-command marker and no npm installation on rejected metadata. Plant CR/LF, ANSI, secrets and long/unicode strings in candidate fields/stderr and assert outputTail is the same host-owned ASCII literal, <=512 UTF8 bytes, with none of those inputs. Track only owned child PIDs, clean them and temp dirs, require Linux/WSL execution rather than a skipped native-Windows row.

In packages/moe-daemon/src/delivery/repairPolicy.test.ts import runCheckSession from '../../../../scripts/local-runner/check-session.mjs' (test-only, never production import). Use an EventEmitter child plus Writable stdin and PassThrough stdout/stderr, following the scripts test's checkProvider event order: write callback completes, stdout ends, then close 82 or 81. Pass the resulting outcome/nonzero exitCode/outputTail into the existing run()/decide()/cands() helpers; use the runner convention exitCode ?? 1 only for an infra result with no observed code. Assert the candidate result produces action:'repair', not retry-infra, with the bounded nonempty diagnostic preserved; the infrastructure result produces action:'retry-infra', consumes only maxInfraRetries and retains the existing escalation behavior. A zero infra budget must not prevent the candidate repair. Repeating the same unchanged code failure must never start an infra retry; existing code-repair escalation rules still apply. Do not change repairPolicy.ts or mock its decision. Keep existing C1/I1 tests intact. This parent owns integration/hardening for the split; the broader epic-final native certification stays CQ-R13.

One verification gate, broad because this changes the guest/host outcome contract. Prepare a FULL git archive/clone snapshot outside /mnt/d/projexts/moes with all prerequisites landed, then overlay only these three owned files. Install host-native daemon dependencies there with npm ci --no-audit --no-fund, never in live packages; use the verified pinned Linux Node toolchain for required runner npm rows.
```bash
node --test scripts/tests/local-runner*.test.mjs && (cd packages/moe-daemon && npm test)
```
Require zero failed in all runner suites and full daemon npm test. KI/C7 and new real-supervisor rows must actually execute on Linux/WSL; native Windows can run pure host/daemon tests but is not sufficient evidence. Capture base/dependency SHAs, owned overlay hashes, toolchain versions, log and outputTail for complete_task. Full snapshot includes scripts/docs; do not use scripts-only archives. Shared live dist/runtime files are untouched; no pattern kills, only recorded owned PIDs. Notify CQ-R13/governor of new supervisorSha256 and environment identity, requiring new operator native certification reports and the final documentation sweep. No reused certificate or verified-local activation claim.

Final adversarial self-review, once (load adversarial-self-review), scoped to this three-file diff plus the prerequisite interface seam. Trace each candidate cause to 82 only after the existing protected-blob/ownership checks; verify cache/lock/toolchain/VM uncertainty stays infra. No broad catch upgrades arbitrary environment failures into a code failure. Negative probes in scratch: remove the dedicated candidate catch and confirm real-supervisor/repair integration fails; map generic install failure to 82 and confirm infrastructure rows fail; suppress the all-dir pass and confirm the invalid-second-dir row fails. Check stale/malformed/truncated frame and timeout precedence inherited from host prerequisite, fixed diagnostics without secrets/control characters, no observation claiming the check job ran, and outcome82 cannot ever be passed. Ensure fds and owned child/process-group cleanup occur on errors/concurrency; never signal peer processes. Confirm old no-dependency checks, locks and earlier 79/80 behavior remain compatible, and package/source bytes are unchanged on refusal. If review changes code, rerun the exact gate; report cause matrix, mutation results, new hashes and evidence in complete_task. Wrapper owns Git landing; QA reviews. Do not edit reserved CQ-R13 files or expand production repair policy.
